subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 3: Grammar – Modal verbs of obligation
outcomes: Know what should, must, mustn’t, need to and needn’t mean.
Choose the correct modal verb in a sentence.
Talk about rules and give advice to save water and energy.

tf.why: Yes! You needn’t do it, but you can if you want.

tf.s: “Mustn’t” means it is not necessary, but you can do it.
tf.why: Mustn’t means it is necessary NOT to do it.

tf.s: We use “should” to say the right thing to do.
tf.why: Correct! Should gives advice about the right thing.

tf.s: “Must” and “need to” both mean it is necessary.
tf.why: Great! Both show that something is necessary.

tf.s: “I needn’t to write about it” is correct.
tf.why: We say needn’t + verb with no to: I needn’t write about it.

tf.s: After “must” we use the base verb: “We must stop cutting down trees.”
“We mustn’t destroying the rainforests” is correct.
tf.why: We say We mustn’t destroy the rainforests.

tf.s: Mohammed must recycle the glass bottle.
tf.why: Right! The glass bottle must go for recycling.

tf.s: Zaid’s family should start having quick showers.
Mohammed’s mum has finished reading the newspaper.
tf.why: She hasn’t finished reading it yet.

boxes.q: We ___ waste water. It is very important.
boxes.why: Wasting water is not allowed, so we use mustn’t.

boxes.q: You ___ use recycled paper, but it’s a very good idea.
boxes.why: It is not necessary, so we use needn’t.

boxes.q: People ___ leave the lights on when they go out.
boxes.why: Leaving lights on is not the right thing to do.

boxes.q: Which modal means “it is not necessary”?
Which modal means “it is necessary not to do it”?
You ___ have a long shower every day. (not necessary)
boxes.why: Needn’t shows it is not necessary.

boxes.q: What should Zaid’s family do to save energy?
boxes.why: Walking instead of taking the car saves energy.

o: He should switch off his computer.
He should to switch off his computer.
He should switching off his computer.
boxes.why: Should + base verb, with no to.

boxes.q: Osama ___ hand in the report on Thursday.
boxes.why: It is necessary for Osama to hand it in.

hunt.q: Modal: the right thing to do
Zaid’s family should go to school…

mcq.q: Which modal verbs mean something is necessary?
mcq.why: Must and need to both mean necessary.
We say needn’t write, not needn’t to write.

mcq.q: What is true about Mohammed’s mum and the newspaper?
o: She hasn’t finished reading it yet.
To say the right thing to do
To say something is not allowed
To ask a question about time

mcq.q: Rewrite with must: “We have to stop cutting down trees.”
o: We must stop cutting down trees.
We mustn’t stop cutting down trees.
We needn’t stop cutting down trees.
We must to stop cutting down trees.
mcq.why: Must keeps the meaning of have to.

mcq.q: Correct the mistake: “I needn’t to write about it in my blog.”
o: I needn’t write about it in my blog.
I needn’t writing about it in my blog.
I need not to writing about it.
I needn’t wrote about it in my blog.
mcq.why: Needn’t is followed by the base verb.

mcq.q: Which is the best advice to save water?
o: You should turn off the tap when you brush your teeth.
You must have a long shower.
You needn’t turn off the tap.
You should leave the tap running.
mcq.why: Turning off the tap saves water.

mcq.q: What is the difference between “You mustn’t bring paper” and “You needn’t bring paper”?
o: Mustn’t = not allowed; needn’t = not necessary but you can
Mustn’t = not necessary; needn’t = not allowed
Both mean you must bring paper
mcq.why: Mustn’t forbids; needn’t gives you a choice.

o: We ___ use mobile phones in class.
mcq.why: Using phones in class is not allowed, so mustn’t fits.

mcq.q: Zaid’s family already have quick showers. Which advice is NOT needed for them?
mcq.why: They already do this, so they don’t need this advice.
